paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches, baker. Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD "all the days he was instructed by Jehoiada the priest" (2 Kings 12:2). Notice the wording. His faithfulness is tied to the man standing next to him. And right after that, the text says the high places were not removed (2 Kings 12:3). A good start is wonderful, but a faith that only leans on somebody else's shoulder can wobble when the shoulder is gone.

Now look at the good stuff, because there's plenty. When the repairs stall, Joash asks the plain question, and Jehoiada answers with a chest, a hole in the lid and honest hands, and the work gets done (2 Kings 12:7-15). The text says no accounting was required "because they acted with integrity" (2 Kings 12:15). That's the kind of baker I want in my kitchen. Do the job, do it honestly, and don't make a show of it.

Then Hazael comes marching, and Joash hands over the sacred objects and all the gold from the temple and the palace to make him go away (2 Kings 12:18). I think that's a man who had never learned to run to the LORD himself. That's the big idea, friend: borrowed faith gets you started, but you need your own. So keep digging into the Word, build your own roots, and let the LORD be the One you lean on. The story of the kings isn't over yet, either.
